---
title: "Security Review Cadence"
description: "Pull request security checks, the security review classifier, the daily findings register and the weekly deep review."
updatedAt: '2026-10-23'
---

Tuturuuu is open source and a high-value target, so security review is a default
part of delivery rather than an occasional audit. Three workflows carry the
automated part. People and agents carry the review part, on the cadence below.
No automated result is a security clearance. Each run is evidence for the listed
sources at one commit.

## What runs on every pull request and `main` push

| Check | Workflow | Runs when | Fails on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Secret scan (gitleaks, checksum-verified release) | `security-checks.yaml` → **Secret scan** | Every PR and `main` push; scans the commits in the change | Any finding in those commits |
| Dependency review | `security-checks.yaml` → **Dependency review** | PRs that change a manifest or lockfile | New dependency with a high/critical advisory (GitHub dependency graph) |
| Dependency audit (`bun audit`) | `security-checks.yaml` → **Dependency audit** | PRs and pushes that change a manifest or lockfile | High/critical advisory present at head but not at base |
| Workflow trust boundaries | `security-checks.yaml` → **Workflow trust boundaries** | Changes under `.github/` or `scripts/ci/` | Any failing workflow security suite (`scripts/ci/workflow-*.test.js`, `security-*.test.js`, protected concurrency, workflow config) |
| CodeQL (`security-extended`) | `codeql.yml` → **Analyze (language)** | PRs and `main` pushes; only languages the diff touches (`javascript-typescript`, `python`, `actions`) | High/critical result absent from the latest `main` analysis |
| Security review classification | `security-review-classifier.yaml` → **Security review** check and `security-review-required` label | Every PR event | Reports `action_required` until an independent security review is recorded |

Path gating uses the same changed-file resolution as the `ci-check` switchboard
(`tuturuuu.ci.ts` keys `security-checks.yaml` and `codeql.yml`). Unknown change
sets scan everything.

### Pre-existing findings

The October 2026 CodeQL refresh reported 270 open alerts. Pull requests fail only
on high/critical CodeQL results the diff introduces, matched against the latest
`main` analysis by rule and GitHub's primary location fingerprint. The same
applies to `bun audit` advisories, compared against the base commit. Existing
findings are tracked in the findings register instead of blocking unrelated work.

### Fork safety

- `security-checks.yaml` and `codeql.yml` use `pull_request`, so fork runs get a
  read-only token and no secrets. Jobs install no packages and run no package
  scripts. `bun audit` reads only manifests and the lockfile.
- Gitleaks configuration (`.github/security/gitleaks.toml`) and the scan
  summarizers are read from the base commit, so a PR cannot allowlist or hide its
  own finding. Allowlists are path-scoped with a reason; never allowlist by value.
- Fork CodeQL results are not uploaded. They feed only the new-alert gate.
- Do not enable GitHub CodeQL default setup while `codeql.yml` exists. Code
  scanning rejects advanced-setup uploads when default setup is on.

## Security review classification

`security-review-classifier.yaml` runs on `pull_request_target` from the default
branch. It never checks out, installs or executes pull request content. It lists
the PR's file names (including the old name of renamed files) through the API
and classifies them with `scripts/ci/security-paths.js`:

| Category | Examples | Owner role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ci` | `.github/**`, `scripts/ci/**`, `tuturuuu.ci.ts`, `scripts/git-*` | `ci-cd` |
| `auth` | `packages/auth`, `packages/sso`, auth/session/OAuth/MFA paths, `proxy.ts` | `platform-auth` |
| `rls-database` | `apps/database/**`, `packages/supabase/**`, RLS/policy files | `database` |
| `tenant-isolation` | permission, RBAC, tenant and workspace-membership helpers | `platform` |
| `runner-sandbox` | devbox, cron, coordination, playground, Dockerfiles, Wrangler config | `runtime` |
| `tokens-secrets` | token, secret, credential, crypto, JWT and API-key paths, `.env*` | `platform-auth` |
| `storage` | `packages/storage-core`, Drive, upload/bucket/signed-URL paths | `storage` |

Docs (`.md`, `.mdx`) and translation bundles are exempt. A file list at GitHub's
3,000-file limit is always classified as requiring review.

When a PR matches, the workflow adds the `security-review-required` label and
records a **Security review** check run on the head commit. The check concludes
`success` only when a user listed in the repository variable `SECURITY_REVIEWERS`
(comma separated, set by an admin) has approved that exact head commit and is not
the PR author. After the review, re-run the classification run. A new commit
requires a new approval.

The control cannot be bypassed by the PR author:

- The workflow file and classifier come from the base/default branch.
- Removing the label triggers a new run, which re-adds it.
- Changing the classifier is itself a `ci` change that requires review.

The integration owner must not merge a PR with a pending **Security review**
check. Before merging, re-derive the decision from `main`:
`node -e "console.log(require('./scripts/ci/security-paths.js').classifyReview(process.argv.slice(1)))" <paths>`.

## Daily audit and findings register

The daily `security-checks.yaml` schedule (`17 2 * * *`, the only security timer)
runs CodeQL on `main` through `codeql.yml`, gitleaks over the last three days of
history, `bun audit` on the lockfile, and the workflow trust suites. It then
builds the findings register (`scripts/ci/security-findings-register.js`) from
those results and the code scanning and Dependabot alert APIs.

Each register entry (`tuturuuu-security-register/v1`) has:

- `id`: stable `TTR-SEC-<SOURCE>-<hash>`, derived from the advisory, alert number
  or fingerprint.
- `severity`, `owner` (role), `source` and `status` (`open`, `fixed`, `accepted`).
- `confirmed`: whether a finding is a confirmed advisory match or untriaged scanner
  output.
- `remediation`: receipts such as fix or dismissal time and reason.
- `reference`: advisory or alert URL.

Actions logs and artifacts of a public repository are public, so the register is
redacted. It omits secret values and locations, and the rule IDs and paths of
code-scanning alerts; those stay in GitHub's maintainer-only security views and
are referenced by alert URL. Dependency entries name the package and public
advisory. Never add raw secrets or customer logs to scans, summaries or artifacts.

**Confirmed critical/high findings are release blockers.** The register job fails
while any confirmed open critical/high entry exists. The integration owner treats
a red register run, or any open private security advisory, as a blocker for
production sync. Untriaged CodeQL and gitleaks output stays visible, unconfirmed,
until a maintainer triages it. Record a confirmed code finding as a private
repository security advisory, or fix it.

A source that could not be read (for example, secret scanning alerts are not
readable with the workflow token) is listed as a coverage gap, never as clean.

## Weekly deep review

No extra timer runs this. On Mondays (UTC) the daily schedule also runs a
full-history secret scan, and a manual dispatch can request the same deep pass
with the `deep` input. During the week that follows, the security integration
owner, or an agent assigned that role by the program owner, reviews:

1. The latest findings register: triage new unconfirmed entries, confirm or
   dismiss them with a reason, and check that blocker owners have remediation in
   progress.
2. GitHub's maintainer-only views:
   - secret scanning and push-protection bypasses (rotate exposed credentials
     first);
   - code scanning alerts by severity;
   - Dependabot alerts, including manifests outside `bun.lock`.
3. Merged PRs carrying `security-review-required`: each needs a recorded
   independent approval of its merged head.
4. Workflow trust drift: run `uvx zizmor --offline .github` locally and compare
   it with the workflow security suites; fix or record new high findings.

Record the outcome in the private program backlog. Keep public notes to IDs,
counts and remediation receipts.
